searches.reason: Test whether SASRec’s single history representation mixes current intent with older interests. Seek practical architectures that combine recent transitions, persistent preferences, and learned time decay using observed histories and timestamps. Compare against SASRec across all four datasets using macro validation HR@10.

searches.reason: Investigate whether the training objective explains weak ranking separation, especially in Electronics. Seek alternatives to single-negative training with explicit treatment of false negatives and sampling bias. Training margins alone do not establish validation gains; compare objectives under equal GPU budgets and the pinned HR@10 evaluator.

searches.reason: Explore a complementary transition or item-graph expert that distinguishes plausible next purchases from broad similarity. Build relationships only from training interactions and available titles/descriptions, without pretrained weights. Seek learned routing between sequential and graph evidence; treat compatibility and purchase completion as uncertain rather than observed labels.
